subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit parent-self-only tool denial policy for delegated sessions, and which public syntax and deny-wins semantics should own that security boundary?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the change creates new config/API surface for command and file tools and changes how requester and child session authority relate, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product/security contract.

options.title: Design explicit delegate-only policy
options.body: Adopt a first-class self-deny/delegate-only policy with ordinary `deny` remaining absolute, audit diagnostics, docs, and native/ACP/gateway coverage before implementation.

options.title: Keep monotonic inheritance
options.body: Keep the current rule that child sessions cannot regain tools removed from the requester, accepting separate agent profiles or prompt guidance as the supported pattern.

options.title: Fold into broader delegated permissions
options.body: Defer this request into a unified spawned-session/per-binding permission model so parent-self-only delegation and child narrowing share one API.

recommendation.title: Design explicit delegate-only policy
recommendation.body: Adopt a first-class self-deny/delegate-only policy with ordinary `deny` remaining absolute, audit diagnostics, docs, and native/ACP/gateway coverage before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent is listed for both Agents and Security and has current-line provenance on the central inherited tool-policy paths.
